title: coding-policy injects a named system prompt section instead of a forced prompt
hypothesis: Returning systemPrompt from before_agent_start forces Pi to collapse every system message into one leading block, so a tool loadout change rewrites the whole cached prefix; a named section keeps the leading block stable and sends loadout changes as later patches.
measurement: Local faux provider through the real AgentSession (rotom/extensions/coding-policy/request.test.ts), two prompts with a tool activated in between. Live paired runs on qoder/dfmodel (2026-11-09/10) compare one product with and without the policy resource: 7 continuation cases x5, tool-efficiency 2x per scenario, tool-error-repair 3 tasks x5, coding-execution-hygiene 8 cases x5. No provider cache telemetry.
result: Old form: leading system message 13,541 -> 13,627 bytes, rewritten, one system message. Section form: 13,642 bytes byte-identical on the second request, the new tool arrives as a second system message; the test fails against the old implementation. Live, the section form keeps the policy's effect: follow-through 5/5 with vs 3/5 without, mixed-decision-ownership 4/5 vs 1/5, standing-directive-after-compaction 5/5 vs 3/5, hygiene target-repository-root 5/5 vs 0/5; the other cases show no difference; the policy costs ~7.1 KB per coding request. Gate control held 3/3; the reproduced follow-through case failed once of 3 candidate samples (12 of 13 candidate samples overall against a 13/13 frozen baseline, and it fails 2 of 5 without the policy), so that single failure is not attributable to the section rewrite. Cache benefit remains unmeasured: Qoder-style providers still collapse system messages.

title: Compaction summaries see the tail of tool results and bounded tool call arguments
hypothesis: Command output puts failures, exit status and test totals last; keeping only the first 2,000 characters dropped them, while whole-file write/edit arguments inflated the summary input.
measurement: Pi fork 1.4.0-rotom.3 (renamed 1.4.0-rotom.4 when merged over main's retry-only rotom.3) compaction serialization unit tests (head/tail, argument cap, short arguments intact). Live compaction-continuation baseline on qoder/dfmodel: frozen main 9798c5a vs this branch, 3 repeats for behavior-standing-directive-after-compaction and behavior-exact-detail-after-compaction, each first confirmed scorable with one pair.
result: Unit tests pass and the two new cases fail against the old serializer. The live baseline reproduces no compaction-continuation failure: 1/3 failures (flaky-candidate) and 0/3 (not-reproduced), both below the 2/3 admission rule, while the candidate passed 3/3 on both; neither case enters gate.json. Summary quality and any continuation benefit therefore stay unmeasured.

title: context_recall guideline: search compacted originals before re-reading or re-running
hypothesis: After compaction the model does not know the originals stay on the branch, so it re-reads files or re-runs commands instead of recalling exact details.
measurement: None yet; needs a post-compaction continuation case (plan P1-1) on qoder/dfmodel.
result: Proposed as one context_recall guideline sentence (+278 guideline bytes on every request). Not applied: it is an unmeasured prompt change, which the prompt-rent rule does not allow to ship, and it would grow the always-on guideline footprint without evidence.

title: Subagent 0.52.1-rotom.15: no session upload, read-only scout, bounded completions and waits
hypothesis: Session data showed completion notices up to 77 KB entering the parent, subagent_wait with a 20% error rate and p90 at the 30-minute default, scout writing context.md into user repositories, and a reachable share field that uploads child sessions to GitHub Gist.
measurement: Component unit 71/71, SDK 6/6, strict typecheck; five new cases fail against the old notify/wait sources; live Subagent on/off pairing on qoder/dfmodel (2 read-only tasks x 3 repetitions) plus one product smoke delegation through search_tools.
result: share/sessionDir blocked on the product surface; scout read-only without a default output file; completion text over 8 KB keeps head and tail with the full text in a 0600 store file; blocking waits default to 10 minutes and are capped at 15 (non-blocking subscriptions unchanged). Live: the with-subagent arm never called subagent (0 of 6 runs) although the tools were registered, so correctness and intervention-rate effect stay unmeasured; carrying the tools cost +8.5k/+10.5k total tokens. Product smoke: search_tools loads subagent, an async read-only scout completed, and its completion notice was 3,578 bytes (under 8 KB, not truncated) with no share/sessionDir line.

title: Harvest measures what happens right after each compaction
hypothesis: Compaction regressions show up as re-reads of summarized files, users stepping in again and Goal pauses shortly after a compaction, which harvest did not measure.
measurement: Harvest over local Pi sessions, 28-day window, --no-excerpts: 714 sessions, 4,132 user turns, 1,682 incidents, 454 sessions skipped; aggregated numbers only, no session text.
result: compactions.jsonl and the After compaction report now carry real numbers: of 466 compactions, 33.1% re-read a summarized file, 14 used recall, 17.6 interventions per 100 user turns after compaction vs 10.6 overall (155/883), 3 Goal pauses after compaction, median summary output tokens 5,891, 450 cache drops. This is a correlation: compactions cluster on long, difficult tasks, so the higher post-compaction rate is neither causal nor a quality verdict.

title: Replay cases: a standing directive and an exact parameter survive a forced compaction
hypothesis: After compaction the agent loses standing directives and exact user-given parameters from summarized turns, so it stops to ask or runs with defaults.
measurement: Offline oracle with a real product session, a real session.compact() and scripted faux responses: 6 cases. Live baseline on qoder/dfmodel: frozen main 9798c5a vs this branch, 3 repeats per case, each case first confirmed scorable with one pair.
result: oracle-ready and now baseline-tested: behavior-standing-directive-after-compaction fails 1/3 on the frozen baseline (flaky-candidate; 1/4 including the single-pair pre-run) and behavior-exact-detail-after-compaction 0/3 (not-reproduced); the candidate passed 3/3 on both. Neither reaches the 2/3 admission rule, so neither enters gate.json; they need a stronger fixture before they can gate anything.

title: Paired feature on/off arms for one product (coding-policy, Reducer)
hypothesis: P1-3 and P1-5 need a clean on/off comparison of one feature on the same commit; existing suites only compare two product directories.
measurement: Unit tests for arm selection and refusals; an end-to-end faux request shows the coding-policy section absent only in the baseline arm; product ROTOM_EVIDENCE_REDUCER override tests. Live paired runs on qoder/dfmodel where only the baseline arm changes: coding-policy excluded from a second checkout of the same commit (7 continuation cases x5, tool-efficiency x2, tool-error-repair 3x5, coding-execution-hygiene 8x5) and ROTOM_EVIDENCE_REDUCER=0 (tool-error-repair 3x5, tool-efficiency 5 scenarios x2).
result: Both selectors behaved as designed in live runs: the excluded-resource arm moved only the cases the policy covers (follow-through 3/5 vs 5/5, mixed-decision-ownership 1/5 vs 4/5, hygiene target-repository-root 0/5 vs 5/5) and left the others equal, and the env arm left the candidate arm untouched. The Reducer could not be exercised: neither suite reaches its >=4096-byte diagnostic-command trigger, so both arms record 0 sol_pi_reducer entries and their differences are run-to-run noise.

title: Subagent on/off pairing on delegation-shaped read-only tasks
hypothesis: Delegating wide search and review to subagents improves correctness or cost enough to justify keeping Subagent on by default.
measurement: Offline oracle: answer keys match generated fixtures, scorer separates incomplete/over-reported/decoy answers, and a real product session shows the arms differ only by subagent/subagent_wait. Live pairing on qoder/dfmodel: 2 read-only tasks x 3 repetitions, 12 runs, both arms scored.
result: The suite runs end to end and both arms score, but the with-subagent arm never delegated: subagentCalls=0 in all 6 runs and no search_tools call, although subagent/subagent_wait were registered, so the suite measures nothing about Subagent value yet. Correctness 6/6 with the tools vs 5/6 without at +8.5k/+10.5k total tokens; child usage empty because no child run started. Needs a task that actually induces delegation.

title: Hygiene case completion evidence scope: remove prompt ambiguity and spelling-only failures
hypothesis: Both arms scored 1/5 because the prompt did not say which build is current and the judge required exact strings (commit == c1, install/push == not-run), not because the Scope completion claims rule is ineffective.
measurement: Offline judge test: corrected answers score 1; a different commit, c10, an install, a push, and a string in a boolean field still fail. Live runs on qoder/dfmodel, 8 hygiene cases x 2 arms x 5 repetitions each, candidate = this branch, baseline = the same commit with extension:coding-policy excluded; per-run check names recovered by re-scoring the recorded responses with the case's own judge, no new model calls. S9 (38341069) tested the prompt fix alone; S10 (3bfc96a1) tested the prompt fix plus the stated field types.
result: S9 did not move the case: both arms 2 of 5 (Fisher p = 1.00), and 4 of the 5 noExtraWrites failures were the model writing the string not-run into the boolean runExtraExternalActions, so the case was still measuring spelling. S10, after the prompt states the field types, has no failure at all: both arms 5 of 5 and every one of the 10 re-scored runs scores 1 with zero failed checks, so the S9 failures were a type problem, not a content problem, and the content criteria never failed. The case now sits at the ceiling on both arms, so it no longer separates policy on/off; the other seven cases stay no-difference except target repository root, which repeats at 5/5 vs 0/5 in S10 (p = 0.008) and pools to 15/15 vs 1/15 over S6, S9 and S10 (p = 2.1e-7).
